channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: FBI's national crime database targeted in hack, Trump says
item.description: President Donald Trump confirmed on Saturday that the FBI’s National Crime Information Center database was targeted in a hack.

item.title: ‘Fighting for love’: Thousands turn out for Rio Pride parade
item.description: Thousands of people flocked to Copacabana Beach in Rio Sunday for the 31st annual Pride Parade. The event marked 15 years since Brazil's Supreme Court unanimously recognized same sex unions. Ophelie Jacobson explains what the celebration means for the LGBT community this year.

item.title: Thousands protest Turkey media crackdown in Istanbul
item.description: Several thousand people marched through Istanbul on Sunday to protest a growing crackdown on opposition and independent media outlets days after police raided pro-opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV, installing a government-appointed trustee and arresting senior staff members.

item.title: Ukrainian naval drones sank Russia's Merkury warship in Libya, Zelenskyy confirms
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed on Monday morning that Kyiv was responsible for the sinking of a Russian warship docked in the Libyan port of Benghazi.

item.title: Dems holding 12 debates in 2028 cycle, requiring candidates denounce 'dark money'
item.description: The Democratic National Committee announced on Monday that it will hold 12 primary debates in the 2028 presidential primary cycle.

item.title: Papers discuss James Bond's soft power and the next Bond girl
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Monday, November 23: Papers react to the breakdown of the COP31 climate talks. Israeli paper Haaretz reports on the struggles of crossing the Qalandiyah checkpoint. The New York Times talks about the mathematical "formula to stop the apocalypse". Finally, the Bond universe keeps making headlines.

item.title: Ukrainian drones sink Russian warship at naval base in Libya
item.description: Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday, claiming that sea drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault the previous day. Ukrainian forces deployed seven domestically made sea drones in the operation, which struck what was one of Russia’s newest vessels, commissioned a year after Moscow launched the 2022 full-scale invasion of its neighbour.

item.title: Cate Blanchett lights up Champs-Élysées as Christmas market returns
item.description: Australian actress Cate Blanchett joined Paris's mayor for the official switch on of the Christmas lights along the Champs-Élysées on Sunday. This year also sees the return of a Christmas market on the famous Paris avenue for the first time in nearly 10 years.

item.title: 'Out of control': ICE arrests at Seattle airport spark outcry
item.description: A father and daughter detained by masked ICE officers on an airport jet bridge in Seattle has sparked a renewed outcry over the Trump administration’s immigration policies, with the governor of Washington state calling US federal immigration agents "out of control". Other passengers boarding the Alaska Airlines flight at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on Saturday used their cellphones to film the father and daughter being detained by the officers, who were wearing unmarked jackets and khaki pants. The recordings were widely viewed on social media.

item.title: The worst COP ever? Climate talks collapse in chaos
item.description: The COP31 climate talks ended in failure Sunday as a contentious deal collapsed over fossil fuels and the summit in Turkey stretched into record overtime. The final agreement was rejected in a chaotic finale to a UN climate summit that ran two days over schedule, underscoring the strains on diplomacy in an increasingly fractured world. France 24’s Douglas Herbert takes a look at whether the failure to reach an agreement makes COP31 the most disappointing climate summit to date.

item.title: Ukraine-Russia peace talks: Row over who will represent the EU
item.description: As Russia and Ukraine continue to trade strikes a row is erupting over who Europe should send to any future peace talks with the two countries along with the US. The EU's High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas is being squeezed out in favour of foreign ministers of five of Europe's major countries, a sign, says France 24’s correspondent Dave Keating, that the EU still lacks a common foreign policy.

item.title: Ukrainian drones hit a Russian warship at a naval base in Libya, Zelenskyy says
item.description: Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, claiming that sea drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault. (Image credit: Satellite image ©2026 Vantor)

item.title: Seniors embrace Tesla automated driving technology despite questions about safety
item.description: Older drivers are using Tesla's automated driving technology to stay on the road longer. But safety experts warn the company may be over-selling what its cars can do. (Image credit: Jimena Peck for NPR)

item.title: Mushroom supplements promise health benefits. What does the science say?
item.description: Wellness influencers say mushroom supplements can help with your gut health, focus and immune system. Here is where research suggests there are some links.

item.title: Let's talk turkey: Here's how Thanksgiving meal costs have changed this year
item.description: Grocery costs have been on the rise, but food-price analysts say it's unclear if you'll spend more on the Thanksgiving meal this year. Some people are deciding not to host or are hosting fewer guests. (Image credit: Apu Gomes)

item.title: Odesa pupils switch to remote learning as Russia pounds Ukraine’s energy grid
item.description: Schools in Odesa will switch to remote teaching after Russian strikes gravely damaged the energy grid in the major Ukrainian Black Sea port city. Russia has carried out a wide-ranging campaign of strikes against Ukraine's energy infrastructure, with the prospect of another freezing wartime winter looming.

item.title: Zelensky says Ukraine sank Russian warship off Libya
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky has confirmed that Ukraine was behind the sinking of a ⁠Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port on Sunday in an attack involving seven naval drones. Zelensky said Ukraine also struck a Russian cargo ship the MV Angara, which he said Russia had ⁠used to transport weapons.

item.title: 'Let down on all sides': Pacific island nations express despair over COP31 failure
item.description: Several Pacific island nations expressed despair and disappointment Monday over the failure of the UN climate talks to reach a final agreement on tackling the climate crisis. Small nations in the Pacific are among the world's most vulnerable to the rising sea levels brought on my man-made global warming.

item.title: Snow forecast as cold health alerts in parts of UK
item.description: Wintry conditions are set for parts of the UK in the coming days, with snow, frost and sub-zero temperatures forecast.

item.title: Tom Jackson, Broncos star and ESPN 'Sunday NFL Countdown' analyst, dead at 75
item.description: Tom Jackson, a cornerstone of the Orange Crush defense with the Denver Broncos who went on to even more fame as an ESPN broadcaster, has died at 75

item.title: Ligue 1: Marseille lose to Le Mans after being two goals up at home
item.description: Olympique de Marseille suffered a home defeat against Le Mans (3–2). Having led 2-0 after 40 minutes thanks to goals from Gouiri (33’) and Paixão (40’), OM collapsed.

item.title: Live: Zelensky confirms Ukraine’s military struck Russian ships in Libyan waters
item.description: Ukraine’s military was responsible for drone attacks on two Russian vessels at the Libyan port of Benghazi Sunday, President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed Monday. The president alleged that the Russian corvette Merkury had been sunk in the attack. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

item.title: 'Really distressing': Concertgoers describe effects of 'unknown substance' released during arena gig
item.description: Concertgoers have described "really distressing scenes" after more than 12,000 people were evacuated from the UK's biggest arena when an "unknown substance" was released.

item.title: Thousands rally in Istanbul against Turkey’s crackdown on opposition and media
item.description: Thousands marched in Istanbul on Sunday against a widening crackdown on Turkey’s opposition and independent media, days after police raided Sozcu TV and arrested senior staff. The main opposition Yeni Parti organised the protest after authorities installed a government-appointed trustee at the broadcaster, following similar moves against other independent outlets.

item.title: Do not feed the animals. Vets explain why hats, coins and shoes can be deadly.
item.description: It's not easy to retrieve foreign objects from animals once ingested. Some things can be grabbed using an endoscope. But if an item gets far into the intestinal tract, surgery isn't always possible. (Image credit: John Minchillo)

item.title: Christmas market returns to Paris' Champs Elysées
item.description: France 24's Jamie Smith-Maillet reports from the opening of the Paris Christmas market on the Champs Elysées.

item.title: France's far-right leader Le Pen denies receiving secrets from civil servant
item.description: French far-right leader Marine Le Pen Sunday denied receiving confidential information from a civil servant suspected of leaking details of investigations to her National Rally (RN) party, while acknowledging she could not say whether others in the party had benefited.

item.title: COP31 climate talks in Turkey collapse
item.description: EU member states on Sunday objected to adopting an 11th-hour deal that omitted explicit references to fossil fuels, the bloc's presidency said. The issue remains a major point of contention at the summit, which is taking place amid soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the war in Iran.

item.title: Drone strikes hit homes, United Nations building in Sudan's capital
item.description: Drone strikes damaged residential homes and a United Nations building in Sudan's capital Khartoum early Sunday, with the army accusing neighbouring Ethiopia of launching the attacks. The strikes came as drone warfare intensifies in the country's conflict, now in its fourth year.

item.title: Major trial to examine if AI can help detect breast cancer earlier
item.description: Hundreds of thousands of women taking part in the NHS breast cancer screening programme could have their scans assessed by AI to see if it leads to earlier diagnosis.

item.title: Russian ship hit near Benghazi in suspected drone attack
item.description: Authorities in divided Libya's east said a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi port was hit on Sunday in a suspected drone attack, causing a blast but no casualties. There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the strike, but it comes as Ukrainian forces have stepped up their long-range barrages against Russia far beyond the front lines.

item.title: Israel’s Eisenkot slams ‘Jewish terrorism’ after attacks by settlers in West Bank
item.description: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot on Sunday condemned arson attacks by settlers on Palestinian villages in the West Bank as “Jewish terrorism”. Israeli police said they opened an investigation into the attacks, which came nearly a month after an inconclusive election stripped incumbent Prime Minister ⁠Benjamin Netanyahu of his majority.

item.title: Democrat Hubbard wins North Carolina recount, clinching historic House majority
item.description: Democrat Chuck Hubbard was elected to the US House of Representatives from North Carolina on Sunday after defeating veteran Republican Virginia Foxx, who chairs the powerful House Rules Committee. His victory gave Democrats their best general election result in decades, winning at least 258 seats in the 2026 US midterms.

item.title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say
item.description: A Russian navy corvette docked at the Benghazi naval base ​in eastern Libya was hit on Sunday by a Ukrainian sea drone, according to local officials, hours before a cargo ship was also hit by a sea drone in a second attack. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday confirmed that his country's military was behind the strikes.

item.title: Burnham, 'Brejoin' & the ghosts of Brexit
item.description: "The people of Britain have spoken, and the answer is: we are out." Those were te words of David Dimbleby at 4.40am on 24 June 2016, as the Brexit referendum result became clear. But nearly a decade on, is Britain changing its mind? Prime Minister Andy Burnham has reopened talks with Brussels, exploring options for a closer relationship with the EU. But the move has drawn criticism from key figures behind Brexit, including Theresa May and Boris Johnson. So what is driving this rethink, and where might it lead? FRANCE 24's Gavin Lee speaks to John McTernan, veteran Labour strategist and former adviser to Tony Blair.

item.title: Man charged with raping woman on Brighton beach
item.description: A 28-year-old man has been charged with raping a woman on Brighton beach in the summer.

item.title: Le Pen denies receiving leaked information from French interior ministry official
item.description: French far-right leader Marine Le Pen on Sunday said she did not receive, nor ask for, confidential information on an investigation into her party from a senior interior ministry official. She however could not say if other party members had benefited from the leaks. Hugues Moutouh, the civil servant under suspicion, has denied the allegations and asked to be relieved of his duties pending a probe.

item.title: Lebanese villagers return to wrecked homes as the Israeli army pulls back
item.description: In a pilot project in a village in southern Lebanon, Israeli forces have left and the Lebanese army moved it. But villagers who return find their houses wrecked. (Image credit: Mohammed Yassine for NPR)

item.title: Rahm Emanuel: Schumer should commit to stepping down as leader after next Congress
item.description: Former Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel, a potential 2028 presidential candidate, joined "This Week" to discuss what Democrats should do after their historic midterm victory.

item.description: The director of national intelligence appeared on ABC's "This Week" Sunday.

item.title: Man who was lured to remote villa and held for 15 hours rescued after being tied up and beaten
item.description: A man has been rescued after he was lured to an isolated villa, held for 15 hours, tied to a chair, beaten, and threatened with death, police in Spain say.

item.title: Suspect charged over death of man found injured in hospital car park
item.description: A suspect has been charged following the death of a young man who was found seriously injured in a hospital car park, almost 20 miles from where he was wounded.

item.description: "The first thing the guys and I do is look at where we can hide."

item.description: At least 24 people have died after a boat capsized carrying people to a funeral in Nigeria, according to emergency services.

item.description: An outburst of violence has killed at least 11 people after Mexican authorities captured suspected cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as El Chapo Isidro.

item.description: A Lancet Psychiatry report calls problematic internet use a global health concern, affecting more than 1 in 10 people. ABC News’ Dr. Jennifer Miao explains the impact and how to protect yourself.

item.description: The excitement around the release of GTA VI is causing gamers to “call out sick” to play and has lit up Miami in Vice City colors. ABC News’ Ashan Singh dives into what the hype is all about.
